drafted_from: workflow:check-my-code-against-my-rules's own file, tools/workflows/recipes/check-my-code-against-my-rules.json (its wake, definition and steps), and tool:check-an-archive-against-my-rules.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Check this repository against my rules every hour." The AI turns on workflow:check-my-code-against-my-rules's wake hourly with the repository's archive address and your rules as the switch's input. Each hour its newest commit is checked, and you are told only when something breaks a rule.
no_lists_because: It keeps nothing: the archive, the rules and the recorded findings are the switch's input, and a run that finds something tells one notice.
instructions: 1. Turn on this workflow's wake hourly once per repository, each switch with its own input: archive (the https address of the repository's archive, such as its host's archive of a branch), rules, and recorded when some findings are already written down.

2. To catch callers of names another repository retired, add subjects_from to the input: was (that repository's archive at the older commit), now (its archive today), path_matches, pattern and capture naming where and how a name is declared; a rule then collects from that subject by name.
3. Read each notice that comes: its body counts the findings; a finding whose name has a recorded new home says where it moved.

worked_examples.title: A commit that still calls a retired tool is told to the person
worked_examples.ask: (the hourly due-time fact arrived for a repository whose switch input names its archive and a rule against retired tool ids)

rules.why: A retirement is done only when every caller has moved.

worked_examples.given: The archive holds one file calling tool:gone, an id the older tools archive declared and the newest one does not.
